title: Chargeback and Negative Balance Terms of the Keyturn Host Payout Account
content:
Where a guest charges money back, or where what the host owes has left the Keyturn Host Payout Account standing below zero, the share held or recovered and the time the marketplace has to recover it are terms of the schedule the account settles under.

## Terms by schedule

| Payout schedule | Chargeback hold share | Chargeback recovery window | Negative balance grace | Recovery share of later earnings |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard | 100 percent | 90 days | 14 days | 100 percent |
| Weekly Batch | 100 percent | 90 days | 14 days | 100 percent |
| Express | 100 percent | 120 days | 10 days | 100 percent |
| Instant | 100 percent | 120 days | 7 days | 100 percent |
| Fleet Settlement | 50 percent | 180 days | 30 days | 50 percent |
| Reserve-Backed Settlement | 25 percent | 210 days | 45 days | 35 percent |

## The four terms

1. The **chargeback hold share** is the share of the disputed sum held back against the host while a guest chargeback is disputed. It stands at 100 percent on the first four schedules, at 50 percent on the Keyturn Fleet Settlement Schedule and at 25 percent on the Keyturn Reserve-Backed Settlement Schedule.
2. The **chargeback recovery window** is the calendar days the marketplace has to recover a chargeback from the host, running from 90 days on the Keyturn Standard Payout Schedule to 210 days on the Keyturn Reserve-Backed Settlement Schedule.
3. The **negative balance grace** is the calendar days a negative balance may stand before recovery begins.
4. The **recovery share of later earnings** is the share of each later earning taken to clear a negative balance.

The two settlement schedules are the ones that differ most from the rest: a Keyturn Fleet Settlement Schedule account is given 30 days of grace and has half of each later earning taken, and a Keyturn Reserve-Backed Settlement Schedule account is given 45 days and has 35 percent taken.
